info.title: Credential Broker
info.description: Owner-scoped credential metadata for the OpenRegister credential broker. Each object carries only a handle to a stored secret (name, provider, owner, allowedApps) — never the secret value itself, which lives in the Nextcloud credential vault (ICredentialsManager) keyed by the object UUID. Materialised into OpenRegister by the credential-broker-service Repair step (OR does not self-import its own register JSON at boot — ADR-037).

x-openregister.description: Foundational credential-metadata register shipped by OpenRegister for the credential broker (credential-broker chain). The provider catalogue and the outbound-broker code live outside this descriptor (lib/Settings/credential-providers.json + the credential-broker-service phase).

credential-broker.title: Credential Broker
credential-broker.description: Owner-scoped credential metadata. One object per stored credential; the secret is NOT here — it lives in the Nextcloud vault keyed by the object UUID.

credential.title: Credential
credential.summary: Owner-scoped metadata for a brokered credential — a handle, never the secret.
credential.description: Metadata for a secret the credential broker holds on a user's behalf. Carries a name, the catalogue provider it targets, the owning user, and the app ids permitted to use it. MUST NOT contain the secret value: the token is stored in the Nextcloud credential vault (ICredentialsManager), encrypted at rest, keyed by this object's UUID. No property here is secret-bearing, so the metadata is safe to list, export, audit, and query.

name.description: Human-readable name the owner gives the credential (e.g. "GitHub publisher").
name.title: Name

provider.description: Catalogue provider identifier the credential targets (e.g. "github", "gitlab") — a key in the read-only lib/Settings/credential-providers.json catalogue.
provider.title: Provider

owner.description: The owning user (OR-resolved owner). Per-user: only the owner may read, use, or manage the credential. The paired secret is stored per-user in the Nextcloud vault, never in this object.
owner.title: Owner

allowedApps.description: App ids the owner has permitted to use this credential via the broker (the per-app allow-list the broker enforces).
allowedApps.title: Allowed Apps
